What is a Rectangle?

A rectangle is a four-sided polygon with opposite sides equal in length and all the internal angles equal to 90 degrees.

What is the area of a Rectangle?

Unit Square

A unit square is a square with side length equal to 1 unit.

The area of a rectangle is the region enclosed within its four sides.

It is also the number of unit squares that can fit into a rectangle.

Move the sliders to create a rectangle occupying an area of 54 unit squares.

Area of Rectangle

General Formula

Square Units

The area of a rectangle is measured in square units (square centimeters, square inches, square feet, and so on).

Example :

Area 
= 4 cm × 3 cm
= 12 sq cm

Area of a rectangle =Length×Width

The area obtained is measured in square units.

Illustrative Example

Find the area of a rectangle whose length and width are 3 m and 2 m, respectively.

Solution:

Length of the rectangle = 3 m

Width of the rectangle = 2 m

Area of the rectangle
 = Length x Width
 = 3 m x 2 m = 6 sq m

Area Using Diagonal

The length of a diagonal can be calculated using the Pythagorean theorem.

d2 = l2 + w2

From this,

w = √ d2 - l2

Area = l × w = l × √ d2 - l2

Similarly,

Area = w × √ d2 - l2

Illustrative Example

Find the area of a rectangle whose length and diagonal are 4 m and 5 m, respectively.

Solution:

Length of the rectangle = 4 m

Width of the rectangle = 5 m

Area 
= l × √ d2 - l2
= 4 × √ 52 - 42 sq m
= 4 × 3 sq m
= 12 sq m
